The song references the "Winter King" (Frederick V of the Palatinate) and Ferdinand (Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II), with the central dispute being Frederick’s brief rule in Bohemia after the Bohemian Revolt of 1618–1620.  
The lyrics emphasize that "Ferdinand alone can be Bohemia’s lawful king," pointing to a contested succession — Frederick was elected by the Protestant estates, but Ferdinand claimed hereditary right.  
This conflict over legitimate succession triggered the early phase of the Thirty Years’ War.  

Religious conflict (B) was indeed part of the broader context, but the song’s explicit focus is on who is the *lawful king*, making succession the primary underlying issue here.  

Final answer: (A)
